title: Correcting the Email
script: Iqbal: [thoughtful] Did you see the email? The director praised the onboarding redesign in front of the whole department this morning.
Farah: I saw it. She mentioned my name specifically, which is the part I can't quite sit with.
Iqbal: [carefully] Why not? You led the presentation.
Farah: I presented it, yes, but the redesign itself, the actual structure, came almost entirely from Dimas's draft, back before he went on leave.
Iqbal: [reflective] Dimas isn't even around to see the email. Nobody's going to correct the record over a wording mistake.
Farah: That's exactly what worries me. If nobody corrects it, this becomes the version of events everyone quietly accepts.
Iqbal: [honestly] You did plenty of work refining it, though. It's not as if you're taking credit for something you never touched.
Farah: I refined it, I agree, but refining someone else's foundation isn't the same as building it, and the email makes it sound like the second thing.
Iqbal: [gently] So what exactly are you proposing? Reply-all with a correction?
Farah: Nothing that dramatic. I'll just reply privately to the director, thank her, and mention that the core structure was Dimas's contribution before he left.
Iqbal: [calmly] That could easily look like false modesty, you realize, especially since nobody's forcing you to say anything.
Farah: I've thought about that too, and honestly, I'd rather risk looking falsely modest than let credit settle somewhere it didn't actually belong.
Iqbal: [encouraging] Would you still send that message if the director never brought it up publicly at all?
Farah: Yes, probably even more so, since there'd be no audience to perform the gesture in front of.
Iqbal: [seriously] I don't think I would have thought to send that message at all, if I'm being honest with myself.
Farah: Most people wouldn't, and I don't think that makes anyone dishonest, exactly, just a little less careful about where credit quietly drifts.
Iqbal: Send it, then. And when Dimas is back, tell him yourself, before the email version becomes the only one anyone remembers.
Farah: I will. It's a small correction, but I'd rather make it now than explain it away later.

quiz.question: What did the director's email praise?
options: A marketing campaign
A budget proposal
A hiring decision
The onboarding redesign, mentioning Farah's name specifically
quiz.explanation: The director praised the onboarding redesign in front of the whole department and mentioned Farah's name specifically.

quiz.question: Why is Farah uneasy about receiving that credit?
options: She wasn't involved in the project at all
She dislikes public praise in general
The core structure came almost entirely from Dimas's draft before he went on leave
The director made a factual error about the project's timeline
quiz.explanation: Farah explains that the actual structure came almost entirely from Dimas's draft, before he went on leave.

quiz.question: What does Farah decide to do about it?
options: Reply privately to the director and mention Dimas's contribution
Reply-all to correct the record publicly
Say nothing and let it go
Ask Dimas to complain himself
quiz.explanation: She plans to reply privately to the director, thank her, and mention that the core structure was Dimas's contribution.

quiz.question: What does Iqbal warn Farah's message might look like?
options: An attempt to get promoted
An attack on the director
A complaint about workload
False modesty
quiz.explanation: Iqbal warns that her message could easily look like false modesty since nobody is forcing her to say anything.

quiz.question: Would Farah still send the message if the praise had never been public?
options: Yes, probably even more so, since there would be no audience for the gesture
No, she would only bother if others were watching
She isn't sure
She would wait for Dimas to ask her to
quiz.explanation: Farah says she would send it even more readily without an audience, since there would be nothing to perform in front of.

quiz.question: Why is Farah uncomfortable with the director's praise?
options: The trouble is, my team has a standing Monday tradition of ordering food together
The praised redesign was built mainly on Dimas's earlier structure.
Updates listed quantities received and remaining needs rather than faces.
The team should remove that person's image from the material.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The praised redesign was built mainly on Dimas's earlier structure.

quiz.question: How does Iqbal initially minimise the attribution problem?
options: I could have simply said yes, diet
They feared less personal information would weaken accountability.
He calls it a wording mistake because Dimas is absent.
Aid must not depend on revealing identity, diagnosis, or hardship.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He calls it a wording mistake because Dimas is absent.

quiz.question: What distinction does Farah make about her own contribution?
options: Instead, almost without deciding to, I told the truth, that I was fasting
Refining a design is different from creating its foundation.
Financial reports, receipts, inventory counts, and independent review.
Use only necessary details covered by specific consent.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Refining a design is different from creating its foundation.

quiz.question: How does she plan to correct the record without making a spectacle?
options: What unsettled me wasn't the questions themselves
She will privately tell the director that Dimas created the core structure.
More recipients collected support directly and volunteers heard fewer rumours.
Audited figures, clear procedures, and responsible reporting.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: She will privately tell the director that Dimas created the core structure.

quiz.question: Why would she correct the credit even if the praise were private?
options: The fasting itself hasn't changed at all
It must not take their privacy, voice, or right to receive help quietly.
Accuracy matters independently of receiving public approval for honesty.
Crowding does not replace guardian permission and appropriate safeguards.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Accuracy matters independently of receiving public approval for honesty.
